\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھولنا} (phūlnā)}{پھولنا (phūlnā)}]{\ur{پھولنا} (phūlnā) — to swell up; to puff up}

\label{lesson:UR-C470-phulna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for phlegm, then the Urdu for catarrh.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھولنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھولنا}} — \emph{phūlnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to swell up; to puff up\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{گرم} \ur{پانی} \ur{میں} \ur{چاول} \ur{پھول} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{garm pānī meṅ chāval phūl gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The rice swelled up in the hot water.
\end{quote}

Past (it …): \ur{وہ} \ur{روٹی} \ur{پھول} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh roṭī phūl gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھولنا}} (\emph{phūlnā}) is inherited from Sanskrit \emph{phúllati}, \textquotedblleft{}expands, opens like a flower\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9093); \textbf{\ur{پھول}}, \textquotedblleft{}a flower\textquotedblright{}, is from the same family.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phūlnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phūlnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{garm pānī meṅ chāval phūl gae.} — The rice swelled up in the hot water.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for phlegm, then the Urdu for catarrh, then say \emph{phūlnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{پھولنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To swell up; to puff up\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دم} (dam)}{دم (dam)}]{\ur{دم} (dam) — breath; stamina}

\label{lesson:UR-C470-dam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for catarrh, then the Urdu for to swell up.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دم}}
\textbf{\ur{دم}} — \emph{dam} — \textquotedblleft{}breath; stamina\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سیڑھی} \ur{چڑھ} \ur{کر} \ur{میرا} \ur{دم} \ur{پھول} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sīṛhī chaṛh kar merā dam phūl gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

Masculine.

\textbf{\ur{دم}} (\emph{dam}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{dam}, \textquotedblleft{}breath\textquotedblright{}.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پسیجنا} (pasījnā)}{پسیجنا (pasījnā)}]{\ur{پسیجنا} (pasījnā) — to break into a sweat}

\label{lesson:UR-C470-pasijna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to swell up, then the Urdu for stamina.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پسیجنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پسیجنا}} — \emph{pasījnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to break into a sweat\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{گرمی} \ur{سے} \ur{اس} \ur{کا} \ur{ماتھا} \ur{پسیج} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{garmī se us kā māthā pasīj gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His forehead broke into a sweat in the heat.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{پسیج} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh pasīj gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پسیجنا}} (\emph{pasījnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{pasījnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to sweat\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{prasvidyati}, \textquotedblleft{}sweats\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 8896); \textbf{\ur{پسینہ}}, \textquotedblleft{}sweat\textquotedblright{}, is from the same family.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{غش} (ghash)}{غش (ghash)}]{\ur{غش} (ghash) — a faint; a swoon}

\label{lesson:UR-C470-ghash}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for stamina, then the Urdu for to break into a sweat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{غش}}
\textbf{\ur{غش}} — \emph{ghash} — \textquotedblleft{}a faint; a swoon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{تیز} \ur{دھوپ} \ur{میں} \ur{اسے} \ur{غش} \ur{آ} \ur{گیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tez dhūp meṅ use ghash ā gayā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He fainted in the strong sun.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{غش}} (\emph{ghash}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ghashy}, \textquotedblleft{}a covering over\textquotedblright{}, and so a swoon.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{نقاہت} (naqāhat)}{نقاہت (naqāhat)}]{\ur{نقاہت} (naqāhat) — frailty (after an illness)}

\label{lesson:UR-C470-naqahat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to break into a sweat, then the Urdu for a faint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{نقاہت}}
\textbf{\ur{نقاہت}} — \emph{naqāhat} — \textquotedblleft{}frailty (after an illness)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بخار} \ur{کے} \ur{بعد} \ur{اسے} \ur{نقاہت} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bukhār ke bād use naqāhat hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She still feels frail after the fever.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{نقاہت}} (\emph{naqāhat}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{naqāha}, \textquotedblleft{}the weakness of someone getting over an illness\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}
